text.1: This is a collection of components build on top of angular material to make it easier to use it. Additionally little helpers could be found.
text.examples: Collection of conmponents and utilities based on the angular material library.
text.table: Easy way to use a table, without the need to implement the headers and columns by your own.
text.column: Custom column configuration (columnConfig) is available for:
text.enum:
Sometimes it is hard to handle enums, but it is important to use an enum instead of just using a number or a string.
Here you can find some little helpers, which enable you to use enum for material select or in the tempalte as a string very easily.
text.enum_options: Easy way to use a typescript enum as source of the material select.
text.pipe: The pipe provides an easy way to get the selected key of an enumeration in the template.
text.dialogs: This library provides a way to use dialogs in your application.
text.strapi: The Strapi renderer displays rich text blocks from Strapi (paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, code, images and links). With debug = true unsupported nodes are printed as JSON. Images are loaded lazily; if the content starts with an image above the fold, prioritizeFirstImage = true loads the first image eagerly with high priority (add a preconnect to the image host in index.html).
text.loading_button: Different variants of the loading button. The button calls the given function, shows a spinner and stays disabled until the returned promise is settled (also if it fails).
text.install: Install the library together with its peer dependencies.
text.providers: No module is needed: components, pipes and the DialogService are imported or injected directly, and the table registers its own icons. Provide ngx-translate and optionally providePaginatorTexts() to translate the table paginator. For custom texts provide your own MatPaginatorIntl instead.
text.entry_points: The button and the Strapi renderer are available as separate entry points, so you only bundle what you use.
text.translations: All texts of the components are translated with ngx-translate. Add these keys to your translation files (or provide your own MatPaginatorIntl).
text.actions_example: This example enables the actions menu and the row click via the actions input.

columns_doc.date: type: ColumnType.Date - the value (Date, ISO string or timestamp) is formatted with the date pipe and sorted chronologically
columns_doc.enum: type: ColumnType.Enum, args: MyEnum - the enum key is translated with translateKey + column + '.' + key
columns_doc.number: type: ColumnType.Number - the column is sorted numerically
columns_doc.getter: getter: (item) => value - custom value to display and to sort by
columns_doc.css: cssClass - CSS class for the header cell, e.g. to set the width

options_doc.columns: columns (required) - the properties to show, in this order
options_doc.dataset: dataset - the data; null or undefined shows the loading state
options_doc.translate_key: translateKey (default: 'core.components.table.') - prefix of the translation keys for headers, enum values and actions
options_doc.column_config: columnConfig - configuration per column, see above
options_doc.sortable: sortable (default: true) - set to false to disable sorting
options_doc.paging: paging (default: true) - set to false to hide the paginator
options_doc.actions: actions (default: all false) - { delete, edit, rowClicked } enables the actions menu and the row click
options_doc.icons: editIcon / deleteIcon (default: 'address-card' / 'skull-crossbones') - Font Awesome icons of the actions

outputs_doc.row_clicked: rowClicked - a row was clicked (requires actions.rowClicked)
outputs_doc.edit: editEvent - the edit action was chosen (requires actions.edit)
outputs_doc.delete: deleteEvent - the delete action was chosen (requires actions.delete)

button_doc.function: function (required) - () => Promise<void> | void, called on click; use an arrow function property if it needs this

headline.no_paging: No paging (only first page is shown)

confirm_delete.title: Confirm delete
confirm_delete.content: Do you really want to delete this item?

simple_dialog.title: Simple Dialog
simple_dialog.content: This is a simple dialog without any special features in it. But it brings already the possibility to use esc key to close the dialog.

confirmation.title: Confirmation Dialog
confirmation.content: The service provides several function to handle confirmation. Either you handle the result of the confirmation screen by you own or you give already the function which needs to be called (or not) if the okay button is clicked.
confirmation.result: confirm(translateKey) returns a promise with true or false:
confirmation.action: confirm(translateKey, action) calls the action only if okay is clicked and waits for it:

layout.title: Use layout
layout.content: Well, all the dialogs should look like the others. So you can use a simple component which provides the layout with headline, okay and cancel button.
layout.form: Here you can find a simple form, it is displayed in the dialog, the form is validated and the submit button is disabled until the form is valid.

keyboard.title: Keyboard
keyboard.content: Dialogs extending DialogComponent close on Escape (registerEscKey, default: true). Set registerEnterKey to true to submit with Enter; a FormDialogComponent only submits a valid form.
